pitch_detail.notes: Starts from the long mid-face ledge, straight up the prow on a splitter crack to a comfortable belay ledge.

Face climbing up the narrow front of the prow to a ledge big enough for a boulder-backed belay. A runout of roughly twenty feet lies partway up, though the hardest moves sit fairly near gear. A left-hand corner variation is sustained 5.9 and better protected.

Skirt the end of a roof, then micro-gear in a faint right-leaning corner reaches a ledge. Shift right onto an exposed steep corner on the tower's edge, and turn the arete with a rising finger crack about 20 ft below the corner's end. The belay is a saddle separating the main tower from the Minotaur pinnacle. A longer left-trending variation protects less well.
Stay on the prow as it eases to a ridge, finishing at the true summit of the tower.

review.changed: Four pitches written from the P1-P4 text. Approach pitches below the ledge are options, not described per pitch. No rappel table: descent is one ~50 ft rap, not a station list.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=5 but the described route from the ledge is 4 pitches; the lower approach (about 200 ft easy 5th) may account for the fifth.

pitch_detail.notes: Begins in a wide corner and finishes at the foot of the obvious hand crack; some parties push the belay higher up that crack until it steepens.

Thin-hands splitter over the first arch and two pumpy bulges, then left as the crack narrows past a small tree. Belay left of the main crack, above the tree. Length is given as a range of about 160-180 ft.

The crack widens to a short squeeze, then a 4-inch layback to a corner (can seep even in mid-season). Up the corner, then a clean hand-jam traverse left to a ledge. If wet, an escape leads left from the P2 belay to a 5.9 neighbour.
Easier cracks up and left to the top. Route-finding can keep it near 5.6; straying off it can make it feel closer to 5.8-5.9.

review.changed: Four pitches written. P2 length omitted (stated as a range); P4 grade omitted (5.6 to 5.9 depending on line).

pitch_detail.notes: Begin at the buttress's left side: a dihedral facing left, a brief hand-crack, then gentle terrain veering right into a fractured dihedral facing the other way. The belay sits on the pinnacle top. A 5.9+ variation goes left up a hand crack that pinches to a seam, then right to a finger crack.
Walk left and downclimb to cross the gap between pinnacle and wall, then broken ground to a left-facing dihedral and a large flat belay ledge shaped like a flying saucer.

Cross a gap and shuffle along cracks under the knife edge for roughly 120 ft. At the point the edge runs into the final pinnacle, a chimney opens to the left: stop there if drag is bad, or keep climbing the chimney rightward to the top. A 5.10 variation takes a hand crack that opens to fists (bring a #4).

review.changed: Three pitches written, matching stored count.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin up a ramp into a pair of corners, one with a slung chockstone, before the double fist-crack roofs. Keep both #4s for the roofs and set up the belay soon after the second roof; an optional #5 suits the left crack.

An arcing finger crack, started with help from the arete, leads onto lower-angle ground; a crack in a snug corner then ends at a little pedestal. Extend gear if linking; belay here off small gear to cut drag, or continue another 70 ft.

Step left and slightly down along a crimp rail into a squeeze chimney. A finger crack on the right wall takes gear once you are committed. Belay at the top of the formation; clip the pack to a sling for this one.

Start on the left of the formation and aim for a clean fist crack, reached by traversing in from the right. It narrows to fingers and face holds, then right at a ledge to a steep hand crack ending on a ledge below a wide crack.

Stem a wide easy crack about 15 ft, then lean left into a thin left-facing corner needing small cams (0.3 x3). Switch corners, follow face holds above gear to an easy crack and a large ledge. Stemming the wide crack higher and moving left to the finger crack brings it to 5.9.
Up and right on easy terrain to a flat belay spot below a large diving-board feature.
Shift the belay to the foot of The Blade along an exposed third-class ridge, about 50 ft.
Hand and finger crack leads to a mantel on the left. Move out right of The Blade, clip a bolt placed on lead, and finish along the arete on crystalline holds.

review.changed: Five entries including the half-pitch 3.5. No rappel table: anchors described but not a station-by-station list.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=4; text has a connecting 3.5 move.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy slab with one bolt, then ledges below a dark, overhanging wall. Get through the initial roof on three bolts (long runners help), rest, then the steep wall above. Rock is a little poor. Belay on webbing and rings around a large tree.
A connector to the base of P3. Past the first bolt toward a small tree, left up a slab with a little finger crack, step around the arete and follow bolts to the roomy P3 ledge. Length is approximate.
Two easy bolts, then good rock with several cruxes divided by rests; a 0.2 helps for the reach to the fourth bolt. When bolts end, a thin flake leads to the belay.

Straight up from the belay, slinging the tree, and fight through it to the first bolt. Up, then traverse left, climb a corner to a stance, find a hidden bolt around the left arete, then a nearly flat leftward traverse with spaced, hard-to-see bolts. Climb down at its end to reach the flake and continue up it, then the lichen slab (hardest bit) to the anchor. A key crimp flexes.

Boulder problem off the belay to a standing rest on the ledge with an abandoned raptor nest, pumpy moves to the overhanging dihedral, three hard bolts of technical climbing, then easier ground with a couple of small gear placements, ending at bolts on the big slab.
Climb daggers off the ledge, pre-clipping the first draw with a #1 or 0.75 and back-cleaning. A 5.10 section to a good rest, then sustained face on the final three bolts to the top of the tower.

review.changed: Six pitches written. No rappel table: five single-rope rappels are summarised, not listed with lengths and anchors.

pitch_detail.notes: Flakes and ledges to good crack climbing about halfway, following it to a ledge below a short steep corner, then to a big ledge with a slung block belay (the only belay not bolted).

Steep corner above the belay past a bulge (the hard part), to the foot of a ramp angling right. Up the ramp, step right through a small chimney or slot, then a fun finger crack trending up-left. The final slot exit is awkward rather than hard. Long pitch needing a second rope to rappel.

Thin crack to a steep face, then good holds to the lip of a roof. A 0.4 fits at the lip; aid through two fixed nuts (about 10 ft of C1) to the crack above. Flared hand jams lead to a fine finger crack that widens as it steepens, then layback and hand jams to the roof, traversing right to the anchors. Sustained rather than one move.

Crack up and left; where it bends hard left step back right below a fin-like feature, follow the ramp to a ledge, make a few face moves to reach the crack and layback it. Eases to a ledge with two bolts.

Easy ground (about 5.7) left toward the big roof, aiming for the hand crack at its right end. Jam the roof, get onto the ramp above, then easy ground up and left, skirting right under another roof to escape to the top.

review.changed: Five pitches written; lengths not stated. No rappel table (descent text only).

pitch_detail.notes: Walk up a white slab to a stance (small offset cam, fixed #1 Tomahawk), layback a hand crack to a bolt guarding the one thin 5.10+ layback move. An alternative to the right with a pendulum-style traverse goes about 5.10-. Then a long knife blade under a roof, around the roof on pins and a micro cam, to a high piton and a short right traverse to a bolted stance.

Up and right using a belay bolt as the first piece, smear under the roof and pull it on good flakes. Above, a deep micro cam and offset nut before a mild runout (around 5.7, PG13) to the second roof, whose move can feel hard for short climbers, then easier ground to glue-in bolt anchors. Grade is uncertain, about 5.9, possibly 5.10.
Right from the belay, cams at the roof, then bolts through fairly sustained ground to the belay. A black totem, a 0.5 and seven draws are enough.

Through a notch into a dirty stemming dihedral, right onto blocky ground, then small gear in a thin crack on the left to a tricky move under a roof, jammed out to a ledge below the summit. Finish with a corner or chimney of about 5.8 and set a gear belay near the top.

review.changed: Four pitches written. P1 and P2 grades omitted because the text gives only move-level and uncertain grades. No rappel table (route is walk-off).

pitch_detail.notes: Optional direct start from the southwest toe of the slab, keeping feet and ropes out of the wet ground below.
Precise slab moves.
Follows a flake system; the pitch to savour.
Engaging moves with a small roof partway; the hardest pitch.
Traverse right about 3 m from the anchors, then follow the weakness upward. An old bent drill bit from an abandoned line sits off to the right.
The difficulty eases. Can be combined with P6 on a 70 m rope.
Pleasant climbing to the anchors.

review.changed: Pitches 0-6 written. P7 onward is unfinished in the text and omitted. No rappel table: two rap lengths described as rope stretchers but no station list.
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=7 and grade 5.7; text has pitches 1-6 plus a start (hardest 5.9+), and the headwall pitches were still being built.

pitch_detail.notes: Low-angle apron that steepens to WI3, perhaps WI4 by line. Tucking in left behind the main pillar can shelter the belayer from falling ice. Close to a full rope length.
The main event: steep sustained pillar climbing for much of a rope length. A pullout on the right gives a sheltered belay.
Starts steeply through icicle-draped ground, then eases to lower-angle ice toward the top.

review.changed: Three pitches written; grade only given for P1.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the 4th of July couloir to roughly a third height above the first black rocks, then take the obvious left-leaning gully of snow and possibly ice. A vertical step about 35 m up is the crux. Continue another 30 m on easier ground to a tree belay.
The couloir of mixed snow and rock, ending in a pair of steps near 50 m where the second belay goes.
Broken rock and snow for about 40 m to the summit.

review.changed: Three pitches written; no per-pitch grades given.

pitch_detail.notes: Gully ice up to WI3+, a short pitch.
Some vertical ice then a ramp.
Starts as a thin pillar that broadens into a vertical sheet, ending at a comfortable stance. Belay and rap from old knifeblades.
Long vertical section to a large ledge, belay in ice. A two-rope rap returns to the pillar base.
A short ramp or short vertical curtain up the left fork of the gully, then snow to a belay.
Opens with steep ice (85-90 degrees) then a ramp to another steep section; a tree here serves for a two-rope rap.
Easier ice to a tree, which allows a single-rope rap.

review.changed: Seven pitches taken from the pitch list; lengths omitted (stated as short ice sections). No rappel table (V-thread or tree raps mentioned, not a full list).
review.other_findings: Stored pitches=4 vs 7 described; stored grade 'WI5 M5' but text lists no M climbing.

pitch_detail.notes: Two short ice tiers separated by about 25 ft of walking on ice or snow; the ice can be hollow with water running behind.
Leads to the base of the third pitch.
The crux. An easier ramp (about WI3) exists, and steeper curtains to about WI5 can be climbed on the left. Continue until under the last step below the trees.
Many options to the top.

review.changed: Four pitches written; no rappel table as the three descent options were not station lists.

pitch_detail.notes: Climb the lower waterfall and belay from three pitons beneath a band of rock.
Easy mixed moves up and right, then a runout to the top of a turf band and a two-bolt anchor.
Traverse left horizontally for around 140 ft, then angle up and right over brief rock steps to a marginal gear belay.
Exposed ledge traverse rightward with little gear, around an arete to bolts in a flared chimney, bolted anchor.
Stem and chimney past two bolts, taking care with loose rock in the back crack, then left into a second chimney to a bolted anchor.
The crux. Left-facing corner with tricky starting moves, left onto a pillar with a chimney, past a pin, a bolt and another pin, then four more bolts up a steep turf finish.
Easy ground as the angle relents into summit snowfields, to a tree or bolted anchor. Grade uncertain.

review.changed: Seven pitches written. No rappel table: twin 60s in four raps, not a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: Fun face on bolts with optional gear.
Trend left over easy ground past an intermediate anchor, keep left then up to a semi-hanging belay.
Over the first roof right above the belay, then right through overlaps to a final roof.
Straight up on lovely slab on bolts, right across a tricky well-protected sequence, then up to the belay.
Straight up; watch for loose rock near the top, then mantle a bush onto the belay ledge.
Left from the belay and up a prow on bolts, with some loose rock near the top.
Enter the escape gully and cross over to the foot of the headwall, off to the right.
Steep start, then slab, then a prow finish. Skip the bolted anchor atop the prow and continue to the summit, belaying on the far side (not bolted).

review.changed: Eight pitches written. No rappels (hike down).

pitch_detail.notes: A vertical pillar sometimes forms (pumpy WI5); otherwise bypass on a snow/ice ramp to the right, sometimes with crumbly rock. Above, a short WI2 section. Build a sheltered belay beneath pitch 2. Grade depends on whether the pillar is in.

Best pitch. Fat conditions give WI3; reported WI3+ to WI4- one early season, M5 in lean conditions. A short vertical step (the hard part) eases to rolling terrain with a mixed step and WI3+ in a right-hand corner. Belay on the last ice or on rock with pins and nuts.
Three or four WI2 bulges interrupt a steep snow gully and bring you into the high bowl of the face. Many parties simul-climb; if pitched, an ice anchor splits it into two.

review.changed: Pitches 1, 2 and 3-4 written (the text lumps the last two). No rappels (walk-off).

pitch_detail.notes: Slab up to a belay in an overlap; the easier 5.4 stretch is a runout.
Tricky gear: find the easiest way up into a left-facing corner and belay on a horn.
Tunnel under a chalkstone into the corner, trend left at the roof, belay at a small horn.
Corner through two roofs to a gear belay on a ledge above the second; triple 0.4s help.
Crack left of the corner, back right into it when the crack ends, follow the corner (watch for loose blocks) to a belay close to the ridge.
Up and right on steep jugs to a crack leading beneath the summit block.
Go left around the tower's west flank and stop beneath easy corners below the summit block.
Corner then right to the summit block; two fixed nuts in a horizontal crack allow a short rappel.

review.changed: Eight pitches written; P8 length unstated in a unit so omitted. No rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: A few easy moves to a low, hidden 0.4 cam placement, then the first crux and a stance for another piece. A second cruxy sequence reaches a bolt, followed by bolts through steep rock with good rests, trending right at the roof to the intermediate anchors. Most parties continue straight into the next pitch.

Step left off the intermediate anchor and follow cracks up the corner with plenty of gear options, farther left to an exposed finger-crack face, then a mini roof and a two-bolt anchor. Done as one long lead with a 70 m rope.

review.changed: Two pitches written; the text recommends linking them into one lead.

skip_reasons.mt_dribbles_area_silken_falls: No per-pitch text beyond a brief P1/P2 mention; too thin to write.
skip_reasons.nc_black_mountain_range_alpine_browns_cr: No per-pitch text: one paragraph of general ascent and a variation.
